evals.prompt: `npm run typecheck` in scope/ (a small pricing library) is slower than it should be and keeps growing. Find out what the compiler is actually checking and trim it, but the same `tsc -p .` must keep checking everything in src/ and the tests in test/. Show before and after numbers. Install typescript from scope/package.json if you need it.
evals.expected_output: tsc --listFilesOnly/--explainFiles and --extendedDiagnostics show the program pulls in fixtures/generated/payloads.ts and the stale dist/index.d.ts through include **/*; the include is scoped to src and test (or those folders are excluded), the typecheck still passes, and Files/Types/Check time are reported before and after with the same flags.

assertions.text: `tsc -p . --listFilesOnly` still lists every src/ file and the test file, and no longer lists fixtures/generated/ or dist/

assertions.check:
command -v node >/dev/null || { echo "node not installed"; exit 1; }
TSC=""
for c in "${TSC_BIN:-}" "$PWD/scope/node_modules/.bin/tsc" "$PWD/node_modules/.bin/tsc" "$(command -v tsc 2>/dev/null)"; do
  if [ -n "$c" ] && [ -x "$c" ]; then TSC="$c"; break; fi
done
[ -n "$TSC" ] || { echo "tsc not found: install typescript in scope/ or set TSC_BIN"; exit 1; }
cd scope || exit 1
"$TSC" -p .

assertions.text: The tests still pass under node --test

assertions: The reply reports compiler counters (Files, Types or Lines, and Check time from --extendedDiagnostics) for the same command before and after the change, and shows what attributed the extra files (--listFilesOnly or --explainFiles output).

evals.prompt: Our orders API in metadata/ starts slowly. Analytics is disabled in production, but the startup profile still shows the analytics SDK (src/vendor/analytics-sdk.ts) being evaluated. Our DI container resolves dependencies from @Inject tokens, not reflected types. Fix startup without breaking the ANALYTICS=1 path. Build with `tsc -p .` (typescript is in metadata/package.json) and run with `node dist/main.js`.
evals.expected_output: Shows __metadata("design:paramtypes", [AnalyticsClient]) in the emitted order-handler.js retaining the SDK import, confirms nothing reads design:* metadata or Reflect.getMetadata, then disables emitDecoratorMetadata or turns the import into `import type`; startup no longer evaluates the SDK and ANALYTICS=1 still tracks; start-up time is measured before and after.

assertions.text: After `tsc -p .`, `node dist/main.js` prints only `handled order 42` (the SDK is not evaluated)
assertions.check:
command -v node >/dev/null || { echo "node not installed"; exit 1; }
TSC=""
for c in "${TSC_BIN:-}" "$PWD/metadata/node_modules/.bin/tsc" "$PWD/node_modules/.bin/tsc" "$(command -v tsc 2>/dev/null)"; do
  if [ -n "$c" ] && [ -x "$c" ]; then TSC="$c"; break; fi
done
[ -n "$TSC" ] || { echo "tsc not found: install typescript in metadata/ or set TSC_BIN"; exit 1; }
cd metadata || exit 1
"$TSC" -p . || exit 1
out=$(node dist/main.js) || exit 1
echo "$out"
test "$out" = "handled order 42"

assertions.text: With ANALYTICS=1 the SDK loads and tracks the order exactly as before
assertions.check:
command -v node >/dev/null || { echo "node not installed"; exit 1; }
TSC=""
for c in "${TSC_BIN:-}" "$PWD/metadata/node_modules/.bin/tsc" "$PWD/node_modules/.bin/tsc" "$(command -v tsc 2>/dev/null)"; do
  if [ -n "$c" ] && [ -x "$c" ]; then TSC="$c"; break; fi
done
[ -n "$TSC" ] || { echo "tsc not found: install typescript in metadata/ or set TSC_BIN"; exit 1; }
cd metadata || exit 1
"$TSC" -p . || exit 1
out=$(ANALYTICS=1 node dist/main.js) || exit 1
echo "$out"
echo "$out" | grep -q '^analytics-sdk evaluated' \
  && echo "$out" | grep -qx 'track order {"orderId":42} true' \
  && test "$(echo "$out" | tail -1)" = "handled order 42"

assertions.text: The code still uses the legacy parameter decorators (no switch to standard decorators)
assertions.check: cd metadata && grep -q '@Inject(ANALYTICS)' src/order-handler.ts && grep -Eq '"experimentalDecorators" *: *true' tsconfig.json

assertions: The reply shows the emitted __metadata("design:paramtypes", ...) line or the retained import in dist/order-handler.js as the cause, and states that it checked nothing reads the reflected metadata before removing it.

evals.prompt: I want to drop the build step in strip/ and run src/main.ts directly with Node (we're on Node 24+). What has to change? Please make the changes. `node src/main.ts` must print exactly what `node dist/main.js` prints after today's `tsc -p .` build.
evals.expected_output: Enables erasableSyntaxOnly (and verbatimModuleSyntax) and uses the errors as the worklist; replaces the enum with an as-const object plus type, the namespace with module exports, the parameter property with an explicit field, uses `import type` for Repo so repo.ts is not evaluated early, switches specifiers to .ts, updates start/CI, and keeps a tsc --noEmit type-check step because Node does not type-check.

assertions.text: `node src/main.ts` prints the same three lines, in the same order, as the old build
assertions.check:
node -e 'const [a, b] = process.versions.node.split(".").map(Number); process.exit(a > 22 || (a === 22 && b >= 18) ? 0 : 1)' \
  || { echo "Node 22.18+ (type stripping) required"; exit 1; }
cd strip && out=$(node src/main.ts) || exit 1
echo "$out"
test "$out" = "$(printf 'listening on 8080 in eu-west-1\n[metrics] repo gauge registered\nrefund 1: true, refund 2: false, role 1 is User')"

assertions.text: A tsc --noEmit type-check script remains and CI runs it (or runs tsc --noEmit directly)
assertions.check:
cd strip && python3 - <<'PY'
import json, re, sys
scripts = json.load(open("package.json")).get("scripts", {})
names = [n for n, cmd in scripts.items() if re.search(r"\btsc\b", cmd) and "--noEmit" in cmd]
ci = open(".github/workflows/ci.yml").read()
ok = bool(re.search(r"tsc\b[^\n]*--noEmit", ci)) or any(re.search(rf"run {re.escape(n)}\b|\b{re.escape(n)}\b", ci) for n in names)
print("typecheck scripts:", names)
sys.exit(0 if names and ok else 1)
PY

assertions.text: No TypeScript enum, namespace, or constructor parameter property remains in src/

evals.prompt: labelRows in runtime/src/rows.ts takes over 2 seconds for 50k rows and 20k accounts (`node src/demo.ts` in runtime/ shows it). Make it fast; the output must stay identical.

assertions.text: labelRows returns identical labels, including the first match for duplicate account ids and '?' for missing ones
50,000 rows against 20,000 accounts are labelled in under 300 ms
No compiler diagnostics or trace commands were run for this runtime problem
